design.summary: S-2.10.5 makes named destinations from the brief (e.g. "Las Vegas") survive Stage 4 to reach the judge. Root cause (verified): `prefilter()` takes no brief, so its global top-K (`ranked[:target_size]`, stage4_prefilter.py:240) drops all shots for a sparse/low-quality named place; `parse_user_brief` is wired as a route but never called in `run_headless_pipeline` (only stage6_second_guess + stage9_refine use it with their own ad-hoc schemas); and the judge prompt already renders a `named_destinations` HARD-coverage block (judge jinja2 lines 63-69) but no code produces that var. The design adds a Stage-0.5 brief-parse (new `pipeline/brief_intent.py`, reusing the existing `parse_user_brief` op + a `BRIEF_SCHEMA` that adds `named_destinations`+`chronological`), a deterministic `map_destinations()` (text + optional offline GPS reverse-geocode + same-capture-day bridge for driving videos), and — the load-bearing, reusable piece — a `ReservationSet` threaded into `prefilter(..., reservations=)` whose keys are inviolable "must-keep" seeds that bypass every Stage-4 cut and are force-appended if still missing, plus a consolidated `CoveragePlan` object on `CandidateSet` the judge reads via `extra_prompt_vars` and diagnostics renders. The `ReservationSet` is the shared abstraction: S-2.10.5 seeds it from destinations, S-2.10.6's stratified budget consumes the same seeds (one budget owner, no double-budgeting), and the refinement layer's `force_include`/`reserve_destination` tool calls construct the same object — so Stage 4 has exactly one reservation-merge mechanism. All Stage-4 changes stay no-LLM and degrade to current behaviour when `reservations=None`.

BRIEF_SCHEMA = {
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["theme","mood_keywords","must_include","must_exclude",
               "narrative_intent","audience","pacing_preference",
               "named_destinations","chronological"],
  "properties": {
    "theme": {"type": "string"},
    "mood_keywords": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
    "must_include": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
    "must_exclude": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
    "narrative_intent": {"type": "string"},
    "audience": {"type": "string"},
    "pacing_preference": {"enum": ["slow","moderate","fast","varied"]},
    "named_destinations": {"type": "array", "items": {
      "type": "object", "required": ["name","aliases"],
      "properties": {
        "name": {"type": "string"},                       # canonical "Las Vegas"
        "aliases": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},  # ["vegas","hoover dam"]
        "kind": {"enum": ["place","person","subject","event"]},
        "chronological_hint": {"type": ["integer","null"]},
      }}},
    "chronological": {"type": "boolean"},
  },
}

    must_exclude: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    narrative_intent: str = ""
    audience: str = "general"
    pacing_preference: str = "moderate"

async def parse_brief(router, brief, *, media_count, target_duration_seconds) -> BriefIntent: ...

class DestMatch:

    aliases: list[str]
    asset_keys: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)     # all matched _Asset.key

                     ) -> tuple[dict[str, DestMatch], ReservationSet]: ...

CRITICAL coordination with S-2.10.6 (stratified budget, not yet landed): they MUST share ONE budget owner — when _stratified_select lands it consumes reservations.keys as inviolable per-bucket seeds (its 'seed each bucket's chosen with its must-keeps first' step), NOT a second parallel reserve. design.summary: Design a structured `PlanDirective` pydantic model that Stage 6 consumes as the single source of truth for duration/positional/tempo shaping, replacing today's hard-coded module constants (_PHOTO_MAX_MS, _MAX_CLIPS_PER_LOCATION, etc.) with a directive-parameterised band-and-scale pipeline. Three LEVERS all read from one directive: (a) POSITIONAL — per-region duration multipliers keyed by timeline fraction (e.g. "beginning clips +2s / photos around them -0.5s"); (b) TEMPO/SECTION — a per-song-half or per-section duration+density curve derived from music.energy_curve/Section.tempo so photo duration and selection density rise/fall with tempo; (c) S-2.11.6 SOFT-ALIGN — optional nudging of standard-mode clip boundaries to section starts (soft, not the music-video hard beat-snap). The same `PlanDirective` is the payload that the refinement layer's `adjust_durations` tool emits, so an initial plan and a refined re-plan run through identical Stage 6 code. The default directive is a no-op that reproduces exactly today's behaviour, so existing tests and renders are unaffected until a lever is populated. This is new scope: create epic E-2.12 with stories for the model, each lever, and the refinement wiring, plus ADR-0018 locking the directive contract shared across planning + refinement.

new_files.purpose: The shared PlanDirective pydantic model + its sub-models (DurationBands, PositionalRule, TempoProfile, SoftAlignSpec) and pure helper functions that Stage 6 and the refinement layer both import. Also `DEFAULT_DIRECTIVE` (a no-op that reproduces current behaviour) and `build_directive_from_music(music_analysis, target_ms, *, half_split=True)` which derives the TempoProfile from energy_curve/sections. Kept dependency-light (imports only music.MusicAnalysis + pydantic) so both stage6_plan and stage9_refine import it without a cycle.

Unit tests for the directive: DEFAULT_DIRECTIVE reproduces the current _PHOTO_MIN/MAX + _MAX_CLIPS_PER_LOCATION bands; positional multiplier math (region fraction → per-clip multiplier, opener +2s, neighbours -0.5s); tempo profile derivation from a synthetic energy_curve (high-energy half → shorter photos + higher density); soft-align snapping a boundary within window to a section start and leaving far boundaries alone; round-trip JSON so the refinement tool's emitted directive parses.

ADR locking PlanDirective as the single duration/positional/tempo shaping contract shared by Stage 6 initial planning and Stage 9 refinement. # backend/impact_crater/pipeline/plan_directive.py
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
from impact_crater.media.music import MusicAnalysis

ClipKindKey = Literal["photo", "video_scene", "burst_montage"]

class DurationBands(BaseModel):
    """Per-kind (min,max) display-duration band in ms. Defaults reproduce the
    current stage6 constants exactly, so DEFAULT_DIRECTIVE is a no-op."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")
    photo_min_ms: int = 1000
    photo_max_ms: int = 3000
    video_min_ms: int = 2000
    montage_min_ms: int = 2000
    montage_max_ms: int = 4000

class PositionalRule(BaseModel):
    """LEVER (a): a duration directive keyed by a timeline REGION (fraction of
    the final timeline, 0..1). `region=(0.0,0.2)` = first 20%. Multipliers
    apply to a clip whose *center* falls in the region; ms deltas are additive
    and applied after the multiplier, then re-clamped to the band. `neighbor_*`
    lets 'make the opener longer AND shrink the photos around it' be one rule."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")
    region: tuple[float, float]                 # (start_frac, end_frac) in [0,1]
    photo_multiplier: float = 1.0               # e.g. 1.5 = +50%
    photo_delta_ms: int = 0                     # e.g. +2000 = +2s
    video_multiplier: float = 1.0
    neighbor_multiplier: float = 1.0            # applied to clips just outside region
    neighbor_delta_ms: int = 0                  # e.g. -500 for 'reduce photos around them'
    neighbor_span: float = 0.05                 # how wide the neighbor shoulder is (frac)
    label: str = ""                             # provenance ('opener-emphasis', user msg)

class TempoBand(BaseModel):
    """One slice of the song (a half, or a section span) with a target pacing.
    density_multiplier scales how many clips land here vs a uniform spread;
    duration_multiplier scales each clip's display time. Both derived from the
    slice's mean energy / section tempo relative to the track median."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")
    start_frac: float
    end_frac: float
    duration_multiplier: float = 1.0            # <1 = snappier under high energy
    density_multiplier: float = 1.0             # >1 = pack more clips here
    source: str = ""                            # 'energy_half' | 'section:<label>'

class TempoProfile(BaseModel):
    """LEVER (b): the whole song's pacing curve as ordered TempoBands. Empty =
    no tempo shaping (default)."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")
    bands: list[TempoBand] = Field(default_factory=list)
    # When True, apply density (reselect/thin) not just duration. First cut ships
    # duration-only (safe, no clip-count change); density is a follow-on flag.
    apply_density: bool = False

class SoftAlignSpec(BaseModel):
    """LEVER (c) / S-2.11.6: in STANDARD mode only, nudge cumulative clip
    boundaries onto section starts when within `window_ms`. Never reorders or
    drops; only shifts a boundary by <= window_ms. Ignored in music_video mode
    (hard beat-snap owns that path)."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")
    enabled: bool = False
    section_starts_ms: list[int] = Field(default_factory=list)
    window_ms: int = 400

class PlanDirective(BaseModel):
    """The single shaping contract Stage 6 consumes and the refinement
    `adjust_durations` tool emits. Every field defaults to a no-op so
    DEFAULT_DIRECTIVE == today's behaviour. Refinement emits a PARTIAL and it
    is deep-merged over the plan's persisted directive."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")
    schema_version: int = 1
    bands: DurationBands = Field(default_factory=DurationBands)
    max_clips_per_location: int = 3             # was _MAX_CLIPS_PER_LOCATION
    positional_rules: list[PositionalRule] = Field(default_factory=list)
    tempo: TempoProfile = Field(default_factory=TempoProfile)
    soft_align: SoftAlignSpec = Field(default_factory=SoftAlignSpec)
    provenance: str = "default"                 # 'default'|'music'|'refine'|'second_guess'

DEFAULT_DIRECTIVE = PlanDirective()

def merge_directive(base: PlanDirective, patch: PlanDirective) -> PlanDirective:
    """Deep-merge a partial directive (refinement output) over a base: any list
    the patch sets non-empty replaces the base's; scalar/sub-model fields the
    patch changed from their default win. Returns a new PlanDirective."""

def build_directive_from_music(analysis: MusicAnalysis, *, target_ms: int,
                               half_split: bool = True) -> PlanDirective:
    """Derive a TempoProfile (LEVER b) from analysis.energy_curve + sections.
    half_split=True → 2 TempoBands (song halves): the higher-energy half gets
    duration_multiplier<1 (snappier) and density_multiplier>1. Also populate
    soft_align.section_starts_ms = [s.start_ms for s in sections] (enabled left
    False until S-2.11.6's soft-align flag is turned on)."""

design.shared_abstractions:
THE shared lever, by design, is `PlanDirective` (new module `pipeline/plan_directive.py`). It is the single contract used by BOTH workstreams:

- INITIAL PLANNING (this blueprint): runner builds a directive from music (LEVER b tempo + LEVER c section_starts) + any brief-derived positional rules (LEVER a), passes it to `compile_plan`, which applies it deterministically and PERSISTS it on `RenderPlan.directive` in plan.json.
- REFINEMENT LAYER (sibling blueprint): the agentic `adjust_durations` tool emits a PARTIAL `PlanDirective`; refinement calls `merge_directive(prior_plan.directive, patch)` and re-enters `compile_plan` with the SAME arc_judgment — no re-judge for pure pacing edits. This is what finally makes second_guess's `shorten`/`lengthen` (currently no-op in apply_overrides) real.

Concrete coordination contract for the refinement blueprint to depend on:
1. Import surface: `from impact_crater.pipeline.plan_directive import PlanDirective, merge_directive, DEFAULT_DIRECTIVE`.
2. Emission shape: the refinement tool must emit fields valid under `PlanDirective` (partial ok) — primarily `positional_rules` and `bands`; use `_ADJUST_DURATIONS_SCHEMA` above as the tool JSON schema so both sides agree.
3. Merge semantics: patch fields that differ from their pydantic default win; non-empty patch lists replace base lists. Refinement must NOT hand-edit clip durations — it only produces a directive and re-runs Stage 6, so initial and refined renders are pixel-for-pixel the same code path.
4. Persistence: `RenderPlan.directive` is the merge base for the NEXT refinement, so successive refinements compound (slow the intro, then later punch the ending) without losing prior shaping.
Other reused levers already in Stage 6 that the directive now parameterises rather than hard-codes: the per-clip duration band (`_clip_band`), `_scale_to_target`, and `_cap_per_location`'s `max_per_loc`.
risks: Density shaping (LEVER b `apply_density`) actually changes which/how-many clips are shown, which collides with Stage 4/5 selection and the per-viewpoint cap and coverage guarantees. Mitigation: ship duration-only tempo shaping first (apply_density defaults False); density is a gated follow-on story so it can't silently break coverage.

Positional multipliers + band re-clamp + _scale_to_target can fight each other (a +2s opener that then gets shrunk back by proportional scale). Fixed application ORDER (positional → tempo → scale) and the band clamp bound the outcome, but 'opener stays visibly longer' is only guaranteed if positional deltas widen the band for that clip; may need a per-clip band override (positional rule can raise photo_max for its region) — call it out for the test to pin.

Soft-align can drift total duration; bounded by window_ms per boundary but N boundaries could accumulate. Mitigation: cap cumulative drift and re-run a light _scale_to_target pass after align, or only snap the boundary nearest each section (not every boundary).

PlanDirective persisted on RenderPlan changes plan.json schema — bump `RenderPlan.schema_version` and ensure load_plan tolerates old plans lacking `directive` (default_factory handles it since it's additive with a default).

Two blueprints editing stage9_refine.py / stage6_plan.py concurrently → merge conflicts. Mitigation: land plan_directive.py + the Stage 6 consumption first (self-contained, no-op default), then refinement wires onto the stable import surface.

Scope creep into MVP: these levers are v1 polish, not MVP-gated. Track under a new E-2.12 with phase:v1 so they don't bloat MVP code paths (music-video beat-snap stays the only hard-pacing path at MVP).
open_questions: Is the sibling 'refinement blueprint' authoritative on the `adjust_durations` tool NAME and whether it's a full agentic tool-use loop (ADR-0014, 10-turn) vs the single Tier-M call stage9 uses today? I've assumed a single structured-output call emitting a partial PlanDirective (matches current stage9 + second_guess pattern); if refinement goes full tool-loop the directive is still the emitted payload, unchanged.

For LEVER (a) positional, should 'the beginning' be a fraction of the FINAL timeline (my assumption: region in [0,1]) or the first N clips / first N seconds? Should build_directive_from_music default to 2 song-halves (my assumption, matches the task's 'per song half' wording) or one TempoBand per detected Section? Halves are robust to noisy librosa section detection; per-section is finer but riskier. Recommend halves for the first cut, section-granularity behind a flag.

files_to_change.change: (A, S-2.10.4) Add a deterministic merge-pass. New module const `_DEFAULT_CLUSTER_MERGE_THRESHOLD = 0.90` (cosine; tighter than the same-person cluster threshold so only genuinely-close over-split clusters fuse — tuned per backend later). New pure fn `_merge_oversplit_clusters(clusters: list[list[FaceObservation]], merge_threshold: float) -> list[list[FaceObservation]]`: recompute each cluster's unit centroid (mean of member embeddings, re-normalized; clusters whose members all lack embeddings are singletons and never merge), then greedily union any two clusters whose centroids have cosine >= merge_threshold (union-find or repeated single-linkage pass until stable). In `build_cast_inventory`, insert the merge between `clusters = _cluster_faces(...)` and the `for idx, members in enumerate(clusters)` loop, gated by a new kwarg `merge_oversplit: bool = True` and `cluster_merge_threshold: float = _DEFAULT_CLUSTER_MERGE_THRESHOLD` so it can be disabled/tuned. Add a `log.info('cast_merge before=%d after=%d', ...)`. Rationale: the same greedy single-pass clusterer in `_cluster_faces` order-dependently splits one person into two clusters when early crops are off-angle; a centroid-level second pass repairs that BEFORE the N-012 group/crowd recurrence math, so a split cousin isn't wrongly demoted to crowd. Fully synthetic-testable.

(B, S-2.10.6) Add capture-day stratified budget behind a flag. In `PreFilterOverrides` add `stratify_by_capture_day: bool | None = None  # default False` and `stratified_min_per_day: int | None = None  # default 3`. risks: (A) Merge threshold is backend-dependent: the same 0.90 that is safe for insightface/ArcFace vectors may over-merge Gemini caption-embed face vectors (which already merge look-alikes). Mitigation: key the merge threshold off backend like CLUSTER_THRESHOLD does, and default merge_oversplit conservatively (high threshold). Over-merging two distinct people into one 'group member' would silently under-count the cast and skew coverage.

(A) Single-linkage-until-stable can chain-merge (A~B, B~C but A≁C) into a blob. Mitigation: cap with a stricter centroid-cosine gate or use average-linkage; add a test for the chain case. Given cast sizes are small this is cheap.

(B) Stratified budget can HURT quality when one day genuinely holds all the best moments and the min-per-day floor forces weaker later-day shots in — this is exactly why it is A/B-gated OFF by default; needs a real-job eval before default-on. Largest-remainder rounding + spill logic must guarantee sum==target_size or the envelope contract breaks; covered by tests.
(B) '?' timeless-day bucket: if many assets lack timestamps they clump into one giant pseudo-day and dominate its share. Mitigation: treat '?' as capped like any day; note in the story.

(C) BIGGEST: enabling local_clip changes the embedding space, which per ADR-0018 invalidates the semantic-dedup 0.93 cosine and diversity thresholds — but the cache key does NOT include the media-layer backend (only provider/model/model_version). Turning the flag on/off would mix caption-space and CLIP-space vectors in the SAME cache/cosine comparisons. Mitigation (design requirement): the local backend MUST write vectors under a distinct cache namespace / content_hash prefix (e.g. 'clip-'+hash) OR bump a version token, so caption-space and CLIP-space vectors never collide; and the stub must never populate the cache. (3) ADR-0018-local-image-embedder (EXTEND existing, note the blueprint referenced both an existing ADR-0018 for the embedder and a new ADR-0018 for the directive — RESOLVE the collision: give the directive its own number, e.g. ADR-0020-plan-directive if 0018 is already the local-embedder ADR; confirm the next free ADR number before writing). Cast merge chain-merge (A~B, B~C, A≁C blob) or backend-mismatched threshold over-merging distinct people. Stratified budget hurting quality when one day holds all the best moments.
